notes.1.33: 1.35: rḫ-jḫt, 'one who knows things', a learned man. 1.37 is largely restored and its sense is uncertain. The restored [n] may be negative: 'an opponent with whom he could not contend'.
notes.1.58: pꜣ-jri-sḫr, 'who makes plans (dispositions)', is the epithet of this form of Khonsu. The šmꜣw are wandering or foreign demons.
notes.1.43: sṯꜣ.n, 'drew', is taken as 'was conveyed'; grammatically it may be active ('proceeded to'). The šmꜣw are wandering or foreign demons.

nodes.text: The royal scribe Djehutyemheb came before His Majesty.
His Majesty commanded that he go to Bakhtan with this envoy.
The learned man arrived at Bakhtan.
He found Bentresh in the condition of one possessed by a spirit.
He found [it] [an enemy] [to] fight with him.
Then the prince of Bakhtan sent again before His Majesty, saying:
Sovereign, my lord, may [His Majesty] command [that] a god be brought [...]
Then Khonsu-in-Thebes-Neferhotep was conveyed(?) to Khonsu-the-Provider, the great god who drives away the *šmꜣw*-demons.
Then this spirit which was with her said before Khonsu-the-Provider-in-Thebes:
You have come in peace, great god who drives away the *šmꜣw*-demons!
Bakhtan is your town;
its people are your servants;
I am your servant.
I will go to the place from which I came, to satisfy your heart concerning your coming about it.
Let Your Majesty command that a feast day be made with me and with the prince of Bakhtan.
Then this god nodded to his priest, saying:
Let the prince of Bakhtan make a great offering before this spirit.
Now while these things were being done [by] Khonsu-the-Provider-in-Thebes with the spirit, the prince of Bakhtan was standing with his army, and he was very greatly afraid.
Then he made a great offering before Khonsu-the-Provider-in-Thebes and the spirit [of] the daughter of the prince of Bakhtan, making a feast day for them.
Then the spirit went in peace to the place it wished, by the command of Khonsu-the-Provider-in-Thebes.
